blocks.title: Page surgery without an account
blocks.description: Read, reorder, merge, split and secure — the upstream PDFCraft workbench running inside Astravia, on your own machine, with the document you opened in the workspace.

showcase.user_prompt: In PDFCraft, drop the blank pages from @assets/contract.pdf and split it at every section heading.
showcase.assistant_reply: Four blank pages removed, then the file split at the five section headings — six PDFs, written next to the original. The source file is untouched until you save over it.

items.title: The real workbench
items.description: The tab runs the official PDFCraft web build byte for byte. Upstream's wasm and JavaScript are not patched; only two thin files of ours are added around them.

items.title: Open and save inside your project
items.description: Opening uses the file selected in the Explorer, and results are written back through Astravia instead of a downloads folder.

items.title: Nothing leaves the machine
items.description: The document is parsed locally in the tab. There is no account, no upload and no telemetry — there is no network traffic at all.

items.title: The file is written only when you save
items.description: Pages are picked in the thumbnail rail, reordered or deleted, and the result is captured — the document on disk changes at the moment you save, not before.

items.title: Install the plugin
items.description: About 17 MB of editor files arrive on first open and are reused offline after that.

items.title: Open the PDFCraft tab
items.description: Opening the tab shows the editor itself — no preparation screen, no package to fetch.

items.title: Select a PDF, then open it
items.description: File → Open inside the editor takes the file selected in Astravia rather than a system dialog.

items.title: Save the result back
items.description: The output goes through Astravia, so it can replace the source or become a new file.

blocks.content: Encryption and page operations happen in the browser sandbox, on your machine. A password you type is handled by upstream's code, never sent anywhere else.
Interface language: the editor itself is English only — upstream ships no other language. The tab shell and this page follow your Astravia language.
It selects pages in the thumbnail rail, drags them and clicks delete. An operation is reported after the result is captured, and the file on disk changes only when you save.
